message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line**

On Windows you can terminate a running program with the built‑in `taskkill` utility.  
Below are the most common ways to stop VS Code.

| What you want to do | Command | Explanation |
|---------------------|---------|-------------|
| **Kill all running instances of VS Code** | ```cmd\n taskkill /IM code.exe /F\n``` | `/IM` specifies the image name (`code.exe`). `/F` forces termination. This will close every instance of VS Code that is currently running. |
| **Kill a specific instance by its Process ID (PID)** | ```cmd\n taskkill /PID <pid> /F\n``` | Replace `<pid>` with the numeric PID you got from Task Manager or `tasklist`. Useful when you only want to close one particular window. |
| **Terminate VS Code and all of its child processes** | ```cmd\n taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T\n``` | Adding `/T` tells `taskkill` to also terminate any child processes spawned by `code.exe` (e.g., extensions, background workers). |

### How to find the PID (if you prefer `/PID`)

1. Open **Task Manager** (`Ctrl+Shift+Esc`).
2. Go to the **Details** tab.
3. Find `code.exe`, right‑click → **Go to details** → note the **PID** column.

Alternatively, from a command prompt:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

This lists all `code.exe` processes along with their PIDs.

---

#### Quick one‑liner to kill *all* VS Code windows

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

Run this in an elevated (Administrator) command prompt if you encounter “Access denied” errors.

---

### Things to keep in mind

- **Unsaved work:** `taskkill /F` forces the process to quit immediately, so any unsaved files will be lost. Use it only when you’re sure you don’t have unsaved changes or you’ve already saved everything.
- **Multiple instances:** If you run VS Code in multiple windows or tabs, each runs under its own `code.exe` process. The `/IM` command kills *every* instance at once.
- **Extensions & background tasks:** Some extensions launch helper processes. Using `/T` ensures those are terminated as well.

That’s all there is to it—just open a command prompt and type one of the above lines to shut down VS Code.
